newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi share index edges up on foreign demand.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi share index edges up on foreign demand.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange 20-share index edged up on Monday on revived foreign demand, brokers and exchange officials said. The index gained 3.78 points to close at 3307.67.
Turnover was 13.608 million shillings ($250,000) traded on 344,263 shares, compared to 8.277 million shillings on 189,240 shares on Friday.
Brokers said the trading was exceptionally high for a Monday. Market sentiment was upbeat, reversing a downswing seen over the last month, they added.
Investors bought 83,400 shares of Uchumi Supermarket at between 40.75 and 41.50, from 41.00.
Kenya Commercial Bank traded between 87.00 and 90.50 on the foreign board while National Industrial Credit Bank traded between 50.00 and 50.50 from 50.00.
"There is more foreign participation in the market, wider interest, but shares are unavailable," a senior broker said.
Bourse officials said there were bids from foriegn investors for about seven shares in a mixture of sectors, compared to a trend of two or three in the past.
"I think part of the reason why the market is a bit thin is because some investors have decided it might be worth holding onto their shares now that they have foreign interest," another broker said.
Barclays Bank was unchanged at 110.00 while Standard Chartered Bank closed unchanged at 45.00. Kenya Airways was unchanged at 8.50 while Nation Printers & Publishers eased to 157.00 from 161.00.
In plantations, Brooke Bond gained 4.00 to close at 125.00 while Rea Vipingo Plantations closed at 9.00 from 8.80. Sasini Tea & Coffee was unchanged at 76.00.

Kenya Power & Lighting gained a shilling to close at 125.00 while Kenya Breweries eased to 58.00 from 58.50. Total Kenya edged 50 cents to close at 64.50 while Kenya National Mills eased to 34.00 from 35.00.

The East African Development Bank corporate bond traded 15 million shillings at 99.61 percent while the Central Bank of Kenya's floating rate treasury bond traded 100,000 shillings at 102.7776 percent.
